answer: Split emission by network origin. The ledger keeps an atlas mapping each key to the autonomous system its signed traffic arrives from, and every AS shares one capped reward slice, so fifty keys on a single cloud island split what one honest key there would earn. When a key's route changes, that delta is put on hold: the new AS must stay stable for seven epochs before it earns a slice, so hopping across rented proxies to multiply slices costs a farm more time than it gains.
